stem:
Nyasha owns Nyasha Electricals, a shop in Harare selling electrical goods. Her business had the following assets and liabilities on 1 November 2025.

| Item | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Fixtures | 6,400 |
| Inventory | 5,150 |
| Trade receivables | 1,320 |
| Bank | 2,480 |
| Trade payables | 3,060 |
| Loan (repayable 2033) | 4,700 |

Her transactions for November 2025 were:

- 3 Nov: Bought goods on credit, US\$1,940.
- 8 Nov: Sold goods which had cost US\$2,300 on credit for US\$3,450.
- 12 Nov: Received US\$1,000 from trade receivables by bank transfer.
- 17 Nov: Paid trade payables US\$2,640 by bank transfer.
- 21 Nov: Nyasha paid an additional US\$1,500 of her own money into the business bank account.
- 24 Nov: Bought new fixtures, paying US\$1,150 by bank transfer.
- 27 Nov: Paid rent for November, US\$350, by bank transfer.
- 29 Nov: Nyasha transferred US\$360 from the business bank account for personal use.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the effect of the transactions of 12 November and 21 November on total assets and on capital.

payload.template:
12 November: total assets {{blank:a1}}; capital {{blank:c1}}.

21 November: total assets {{blank:a2}}; capital {{blank:c2}}.

parts.explanation: 12 November: bank rises and trade receivables fall by the same US\$1,000, so total assets and capital are unchanged. 21 November: bank and capital both rise by US\$1,500.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: What was the effect of the sale on 8 November on capital?

options.rationale: Only the profit increases capital; the inventory given up reduces assets.
Correct: assets rose by 3,450 and fell by 2,300; the difference is profit, which belongs to the owner.

options.content: It had no effect on capital
options.rationale: A sale at a profit increases capital by the profit.
The cost of the goods sold is matched by the higher amount receivable.

parts.explanation: Trade receivables +3,450, inventory −2,300: net assets and capital rise by the profit of US\$1,150.

parts.label: (d)
parts.explanation: Profit = 3,450 − 2,300 − rent 350 = US\$800. Capital = 7,590 + 1,500 + 800 − 360 = US\$9,530. Check: assets 16,590 − liabilities 7,060 = US\$9,530. Forgetting the rent gives US\$9,880.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Profit = 3,450 − 2,300 − rent 350 = US\$800. Capital = 7,590 + 1,500 + 800 − 360 = US\$9,530. Check: assets 16,590 − liabilities 7,060 = US\$9,530. Forgetting the rent gives US\$9,880.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the net current assets (working capital) on 30 November 2025.
parts.explanation: Current assets: inventory 4,790 + trade receivables 3,770 + bank 480 = US\$9,040. Net current assets = 9,040 − trade payables 2,360 = US\$6,680. The loan is a non-current liability and is not deducted.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Current assets: inventory 4,790 + trade receivables 3,770 + bank 480 = US\$9,040. Net current assets = 9,040 − trade payables 2,360 = US\$6,680. The loan is a non-current liability and is not deducted.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Prepare Nyasha's statement of financial position at 30 November 2025.

points.description: Correct three-line heading: name, statement of financial position, at 30 November 2025.
Fixtures US\$7,550 as a non-current asset.
Current assets: inventory US\$4,790, trade receivables US\$3,770, bank US\$480; total US\$9,040.
Capital section: US\$7,590 + US\$1,500 + profit US\$800 − drawings US\$360 = US\$9,530.
Loan US\$4,700 as a non-current liability and trade payables US\$2,360 as a current liability.
Totals: assets US\$16,590 = capital and liabilities US\$16,590.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Nyasha plans to buy a delivery van costing US\$6,400 in December by arranging a bank overdraft. Advise her whether she should do this. Justify your answer.

points.description: Her bank balance is only US\$480, so almost all of the US\$6,400 would be borrowed on a short-term overdraft (current liability), repayable on demand.
Net current assets would fall sharply / could become negative, so she might not pay suppliers on time; a van is a long-term asset better financed by a long-term loan or more capital.
A justified recommendation: do not use an overdraft (use a loan or capital / delay the purchase), or buy only if receivables are collected first.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: She should not use an overdraft. Her bank balance is only US\$480, so the overdraft would be about US\$5,920, repayable on demand. Her net current assets of US\$6,680 would fall to about US\$280, leaving little to pay suppliers. A van lasts several years, so it should be financed long-term, for example by a loan or by introducing more capital, or she should wait until more receivables have paid.

explanation: Opening capital US\$7,590; profit for November US\$800; closing capital US\$9,530; total assets US\$16,590; net current assets US\$6,680.
hints: Capital = assets − liabilities at each date.
Only income and expenses change profit; capital introduced and drawings change capital directly.
Long-term assets are best financed by long-term sources.
